statistics.median: middle sorted sample; arithmetic mean of two middle samples if the count is even

protocol.timedWork: Each phase includes the named public analytics calls plus deterministic result-token construction.
excludedWork: x8 fixture construction and CSV serialization

datasets.distributionStrategy: Approved Phase 2 dates, values, categories, missingness, and customer/order distributions are unchanged.

datasets.source: Approved Phase 2 deterministic CSV replicated eight times
datasets.identifierStrategy: Each replica suffixes order-line, order, and customer IDs with -B1 through -B8; product IDs intentionally retain shared dimension identity.
datasets.distributionStrategy: Dates, monetary values, categorical shares, optional-field missingness, and within-replica customer/order distributions are preserved; row volume increases without adding new business behavior or high-cardinality products and dimensions.

observations.finding: Result-envelope and bounded-evidence construction dominates the scaled analytical paths.
observations.recommendedFollowUp: Profile and evaluate safe caching in Phase 4 without changing formulas, decimal and rounding rules, evidence semantics, sorting, or deterministic outputs.

limitations: Results describe this workstation, Node runtime, process, and run only; they are not universal production-performance claims.
The suite is a warm-cache, single-process microbenchmark and does not include file I/O, concurrency, network or database work, application startup, or UI rendering.
JIT compilation, garbage collection, operating-system scheduling, thermal state, power policy, and other local load can affect timings.
The x8 fixture preserves Phase 2 dates and distributions while changing unique transaction and customer IDs; it increases scale, not behavioral complexity.
Product and other dimension cardinalities remain limited by the approved Phase 2 fixture, so this run does not characterize genuinely high-cardinality breakdowns.
The full protocol uses seven measured samples; nearest-rank p95 therefore selects the maximum sample and is a local tail indicator, not a stable population estimate.
No pass/fail timing thresholds or external performance benchmarks are encoded.
The operation timings include deterministic result-token construction and should not be summed as an end-to-end request latency.
